messages:
Taylor (AE): kicking off thread for ACME POC — they want on‑prem app -> Redwood Private. Main asks: where should TLS terminate (their edge vs our ingress), can we preserve client source IP for their ACLs, firewall rule checklist, and any pricing delta if they need static egress IPs (EIP/NAT). Can NetOps + SE advise?
Amy (Solutions): quick notes: for on‑prem -> cloud we usually do one of: 1) IPsec to customer's TGW/edge then VPC peering/TGW to our Private VPC, or 2) IPsec to our edge and use PrivateLink/ENI-based endpoints. TLS termination can be onsite (recommended if they want end-to-end control) or at our ingress if they need SNI/proxy features.
Jordan (NetOps): firewall checklist (minimum):
```
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to Redwood management/control plane (we'll provide CIDRs)
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to Private endpoint ENIs (service endpoints)
- Allow inbound TCP 4500/500 if doing IPsec from their appliance -> our edge
```
If they need a deterministic source IP for outbound traffic to us, they must NAT at their egress with an EIP (or front with a proxy that has EIP). VPC Peering preserves original source IP in most cases; PrivateLink using interface endpoints also keeps traffic private but egress NAT behavior depends on their route table/NAT.
Taylor (AE): Jordan — can you give an example minimal SG/ACL snippet I can send to customer infra team? Also Amy, ballpark NAT cost so I can flag to procurement.
Jordan (NetOps): SG/ACL example for test (send as text):
```
# customer egress ACL / outbound rules
+ tcp 443 -> redwood-endpoints.example.cidr/32 # replace with provided list
+ udp 500, udp 4500 -> our-edge-ip/32   # for IPsec tunnel if used
```
Also add DNS: if they plan to resolve PrivateLink DNS, they need to allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to their resolver and/or push private DNS into their VPC resolver. If they terminate TLS on their edge and forward to us over a tunnel, you can skip PrivateLink DNS.
Amy (Solutions): Pricing/delta: NAT gateway with EIP (customer side) = NAT hourly + data processing. Ballpark: NAT GW data processing ~ $0.045/GB (varies by region) + EIP/hour negligible per long term. If we host a static egress EIP on our side (we can offer as part of Dedicated/Private SOW), there is typically a small monthly fee and per-GB transfer cost — I'll pull exact numbers for ACME once we know estimated throughput.
Maria (Security): Heads up for their security questionnaire: they'll ask for network diagrams, cert chain and TLS ciphers we support, SOC2/SOC3 links, key rotation/KMS details, and whether we accept mTLS. We can provide mTLS guidance and a sample config. Also they'll ask for logs retention and access controls — we should know what to include in the POA&M.
Taylor (AE): perfect — action items: 1) Jordan — send the SG/ACL text and a short test CIDR we can use for POC (can be ephemeral). 2) Amy — rough monthly/GB estimate and note if Redwood can host an EIP for them as an option. 3) Maria — sample answers for the security questionnaire (network + TLS). I'll schedule a 30m handoff call with their infra lead tomorrow.
Jordan (NetOps): +1. I'll paste the SG snippet into this thread in a sec.
Amy (Solutions): I'll DM the pricing sheet and include a line item for "static egress IP + managed NAT" option.
deploy-bot: deploy job #redwood/provision-test-endpoint succeeded — endpoint 10.1.200.45 created for test POC. :rocket:
Taylor (AE): thanks everyone — sending to ACME now and will add the diagram. :thumbsup:
